transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-03-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Kai Rivera (Redwood), Sarah Lang (VertexHealth Head of MLOps), Tom Alvarez (VertexHealth Infra Eng), Meera Iyer (CTO), Jin Park (SRE)
---
[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Olivia, AE at Redwood Inference. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Sarah Lang: hi, Sarah here.
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: Tom, infra.
[00:15] Meera Iyer: Meera.
[00:18] Jin Park: Jin, SRE.
[00:22] Marcus Patel: Marcus, SE — I'll be driving the benchmark bits.
[00:27] Olivia Chen: Awesome. Agenda — align success criteria, go over your workload scripts, decide streaming vs non-streaming approach, and agree timeline for the POC harness integration.
[00:40] Sarah Lang: that's right. Our main thing is we want to validate latency at scale and cost. p95 below 300ms ideally, and overall cost reduction vs our current OpenAI usage.
[00:50] Meera Iyer: also security — all traffic must live in our VPC for dedicated tests, and we need KMS integration or customer managed keys for any persisted caches.
[01:05] Olivia Chen: noted. On the KMS side Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM — we can outline steps. For hosted/Pilot we can do encrypted-at-rest and bring-your-own-key on Private.
[01:20] Marcus Patel: to scope the benchmark we need your representative scripts — the actual prompts, token counts, typical context length, and concurrency targets. Can you tell us volumes?
[01:35] Tom Alvarez: Sure. Right now we have about 120 TPS at peak across a mix of short chat completions (avg 150 tokens) and longer summarizations (avg 900 tokens). P95 concurrent users about 45.
[01:52] Jin Park: there's also a background batch reranking job that runs at off-peak with high throughput, that's non-streaming and sensitive to cost.
[02:05] Marcus Patel: good — we'll test two axes: interactive streaming latency (simulate users with streaming client) and non-streaming bulk throughput for reranks. We'll compare variants: hosted Redwood defaults, a quantized dedicated variant, and a fallback small model for cost fallbacks.
[02:25] Sarah Lang: can you run streaming tests that emulate partial response behavior — like chunked tokens? That's where we see real user latency impact.
[02:35] Marcus Patel: yes, we'll use a harness that supports SSE/websocket streaming and a non-streaming HTTP path. For streaming we'll measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB), median token throughput, and tail latency at the chunk level. For non-streaming we'll measure overall request latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:57] Olivia Chen: a small note on instrumentation: our console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-model time spent in kernel, and trace IDs you can correlate with your own tracing. We'll include an exporter config for your tracing system.
[03:12] Meera Iyer: we need to ensure network egress costs and cross-regional fallbacks are captured in the cost model.
[03:20] Kai Rivera: we'll include region-aware routing in the test plan and show the delta. For VPC tests we'll do an on-prem-like setup, run traffic from your VPC to Redwood Private in your chosen region.
[03:36] Tom Alvarez: for VPC, do you require any IP allowlist? We run through a narrow NAT.
[03:42] Marcus Patel: yes, we'll provide endpoints and certs. For Dedicated we'll likely use an internal peering option or private link; we'll capture setup steps in the docs.
[03:55] Sarah Lang: success criteria — list that out. We have internal gate: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for chat (streaming), 2) cost delta vs OpenAI <= 40% at current volume, 3) no data exfil risk and SOC2 controls.
[04:13] Olivia Chen: we can commit to helping measure 1 & 2; SOC2/compliance we'll share our security pack and work with your security team.
[04:25] Jin Park: audit logs are a must, retention for six months.
[04:30] Kai Rivera: we have audit logs and request-level traces; retention is configurable as an add-on, will include that in the SOW.
[04:45] Marcus Patel: ok let's dive into harness specifics. We prefer to use k6 or a dockerized runner that replays your scripts. Two options: you provide your existing JMeter/k6 scripts, or we supply a small python runner that wraps your prompts and drives streaming/non-streaming modes. Which do you prefer?
[05:03] Tom Alvarez: we have k6 scripts for the bulk jobs, but our interactive client is integrated in-app. We can export a script for representative user flows.
[05:14] Marcus Patel: perfect. For streaming we need to emulate partial event streams — k6 has websocket support but it's clunky; our sample runner uses a lightweight websocket client that will be easier. We'll give both.
[05:30] Sarah Lang: one gotcha — our reranker uses large context, we keep a KV cache per session. The harness should be able to warm caches to measure cold vs warm token performance.
[05:45] Marcus Patel: good point — our harness supports a warmup phase where we pre-populate KV caches and prefix caches. We'll define a warm, cold, and steady-state test.
[05:58] Meera Iyer: what's your suggested test matrix?
[06:02] Marcus Patel: propose: a) streaming interactive: 50, 100, 200 concurrent simulated users, measure TTFB and p95 chunk latency; b) non-streaming bulk: throughput sweep from 500 rps to 5k rps with 100ms and 1s concurrency windows; c) cache warm vs cold: run identical workload with and without pre-populated caches; d) model variants: baseline open model we onboard, quantized 4-bit variant, and cost-fallback small model. We'll produce a sheet mapping expected metrics and pass/fail gates.
[06:35] Tom Alvarez: Our infra will throttle at network edge at around 2k rps, so the runner needs to emulate that limit.
[06:42] Marcus Patel: ok we'll build the runner to respect your NAT/e2e limits.
[06:45] [crosstalk] Jin Park: also cert rotations are monthly for us — need automation.
[06:50] Kai Rivera: we'll include cert rotation docs and automation hooks for renewals.
[07:00] Sarah Lang: about metrics — we need raw token counts, time in runtime, kernel time, network time, and any batching stats. Can Redwood export those?
[07:10] Olivia Chen: yes — the console exports token-level and kernel runtime breakdowns. We'll give a sample CSV and a small exporter to push to your prometheus/grafana or a S3 bucket.
[07:25] Meera Iyer: any quirks we should be aware of — e.g., quantized models sometimes change output distribution; that affects accuracy/regression. How do you measure quality?
[07:36] Marcus Patel: we'll run an eval harness on a holdout set of prompts and compare outputs from each model variant against your ground truth. For rerankers we'll compute NDCG and for chat we run a set of human-review prompts and an automated metric for hallucination/factuality where possible. We'll surface any regressions.
[07:58] Sarah Lang: can we get a short example of the eval reporting format?
[08:02] Marcus Patel: yes, sample PDF/CSV will be included.
[08:08] Tom Alvarez: on the deployment topology — do you support colocated KV cache with the inference nodes? We saw in your docs mention of KV cache management.
[08:16] Kai Rivera: yes, we do local KV caches per node for low-latency, and a shared backing for persistence. For Private we can wire that into your existing Redis cluster if you prefer.
[08:30] Jin Park: we need to ensure encryption in transit between redis and nodes.
[08:33] Marcus Patel: mTLS and TLS for inter-node comms supported, will document.
[08:38] [00:09:00 marker omitted for brevity]
[08:40] Olivia Chen: timeline proposals — quick POC: 3 weeks to run benchmarks and produce results. Week 1: instrument + share scripts and baseline runs. Week 2: run streaming and non-streaming sweeps. Week 3: analyze and present results. Does that align?
[08:55] Meera Iyer: 3 weeks is fine. We need security review in parallel; that may add a week.
[09:02] Olivia Chen: understood — we'll start security paperwork immediately.
[09:10] Marcus Patel: setup checklist: 1) get scripts + token stats from VertexHealth, 2) confirm VPC connectivity plan or onboarding of Redwood Private, 3) share runner images and infra requirements, 4) schedule kickoff.
[09:25] Tom Alvarez: we'll push scripts by Friday — that's 2027-03-19.
[09:30] Sarah Lang: want to call out cost model: we expect a delta vs OpenAI. Please include both raw token cost and end-to-end infra cost for Dedicated (GPU hours).
[09:40] Marcus Patel: yes — our benchmarking exports will include per-model cost by token and estimated monthly cost at your volumes. We'll show sensitivity analysis.
[09:50] Meera Iyer: one more on streaming vs non-streaming: in streaming we measure incremental latency per token, in non-streaming we care about end-to-end latency and batch efficiency. Our acceptance gates differ per flow.
[10:05] Marcus Patel: agreed — we'll create separate pass/fail conditions. For streaming: TTFB p95 <= 300ms and median token latency < 50ms. For non-streaming: p95 <= 1500ms for large summarizes and cost per 1k tokens <= target.
[10:25] Jin Park: what about error injection? We want to see graceful degradation when nodes go down.
[10:30] Kai Rivera: can include fault-injection scenarios in the harness: node kill, increased latency, and network partition. We'll capture failover times and impact on latency and errors.
[10:45] Sarah Lang: perfect.
[10:48] Olivia Chen: recap and next steps: Olivia to send harness template + runner, Marcus to share test matrix + metrics sheet, VertexHealth to share scripts and token distribution, schedule kickoff with infra. We'll aim to start week of 2027-03-22.
[11:05] Tom Alvarez: confirmed.
[11:08] Meera Iyer: we'll loop in security and legal after this call.
[11:12] Olivia Chen: I'll also attach our security pack and SOC2 docs in the follow-up email.
[11:20] Marcus Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with a Confluence page and the runner image.
[11:25] Sarah Lang: thanks. 
[11:27] Olivia Chen: meeting adjourned.
